rounds.text: Shree Vasu Logistics Ltd carries a severe valuation disconnect, trading at an extreme price-to-earnings multiple of 146x and a price-to-book ratio of 21.18x on a book value of ₹34.7 [E1, E2, E59]. This aggressive pricing leaves a massive negative margin of safety of -434.8%, as a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at just Rs 137 per share against a market price of Rs 735 [E43, E44]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF reveals that today's market price aggressively demands a 35.6% earnings growth rate, towering well above the 12.0% assumed in the base case [E45]. The underlying balance sheet is heavily burdened, evidenced by a concerning debt-to-equity ratio of 5.21x where borrowings escalated sharply to Rs 203 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 67 Cr a year prior [E37, E38], accompanied by official flags warning of a low interest coverage ratio [E61] and a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E60]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reached an impressive 53% alongside a 165% surge in profit growth [E17, E21], and the company maintains a strong ROE of 15.6% [E13].
